text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.76% today to $455.07, extending a five-day slide that has wiped out about 4% of the stock's value. The timing lines up with a sharp reversal in oil market sentiment: Brent crude hit $111 after weeks of geopolitical escalation (U.S. diplomats pulling out of Saudi Arabia, fears of renewed Iran strikes, Houthi attacks on infrastructure), but the stock is moving *down* despite oil prices staying elevated. The disconnect suggests traders are rotating away from U.S. refiner exposure even as crude costs hold firm—possibly betting that global refining capacity (Reliance's outsized share in India, broader 93% utilization domestically) will eventually ease margins, or that political uncertainty around the midterms is dampening energy sector appetite.

The broader context: crude staying above $107 is normally good for refiners' bottom line, but Ukraine's ongoing drone campaign on Russian diesel facilities and hints at alternative global refining partnerships (the Rubio-Reliance visit) may be signaling that the tight supply picture refiners have profited from is starting to crack. A refiner's profit margin depends not just on crude price but on what it can sell refined products *for*—and if the world has enough refining capacity coming online or returning to service, those margins compress even with pricey oil.
